summary.headline: KPIT Q4 FY26 revenue grew 1.8% in constant currency and 12% YoY in rupees; management guides FY27 EBITDA margin of 20.5-21.2% as two large SDV programs ramp down.
summary.overview: KPIT closed Q4 FY26 with 1.8% constant-currency and 1.9% QoQ dollar growth, 12% YoY and 5.8% QoQ in rupees, and EBITDA margin of 20.6% for the quarter and 20.8% for the year. Management booked $349 million of TCV in the quarter, with 21% of pipeline in products and solutions. The call flagged the planned ramp-down of two large SDV programs (one with a European OEM, one a surprise stop by a Japanese OEM after Honda cancelled new platforms in April), which will weigh on Q1 FY27 revenue by an estimated 3-4% QoQ. Management guided FY27 EBITDA to 20.5-21.2% and a medium-term 22-24% margin, with solutions and products growing 30% a year.

financial_highlights.metric: Total contract value (TCV) won in Q4

financial_highlights.value: Up 18% YoY in FY26; up 11.6% in Q4

segments.name: Trucks and off-highway
segments.commentary: Grew 18% YoY in FY26 and led Q4 growth at 11.6%. Added 4 truck OEMs and 6 off-highway OEMs across four countries in the year.

segments.name: Connected vehicles and cloud-based connected services
segments.commentary: Cited as the second growth driver in Q4 and the highest-growth area in the industry, per management.

segments.name: Powertrain
segments.commentary: Continued to grow across electrification, hybrid, conventional and hydrogen pilots, though slower than the top segments.

segments.name: Vehicle engineering (Caresoft)
segments.commentary: Expanded beyond software into cost reduction and software benchmarking; positioned for off-highway and cost-reduction work.

segments.name: After-sales
segments.commentary: Called a fast-growing area with 9% YoY growth from OEM clients; Tier 1 revenue declined from a non-focus base.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA margin guided to 20.5-21.2%, after higher investment in AI solutions, products, and new markets; currency movements add uncertainty.
Medium-term EBITDA margin target of 22-24%, driven by solutions and products mix, fixed-price and outcome-based contracts, and per-person productivity.
Solutions and products revenue expected to grow about 30% YoY, rising from 15% of revenue to 40% in three years (management also cited a 50%-plus share as a longer-term goal).
Two large SDV programs ending; management expects the revenue gap to be covered by new accounts, with FY27 sequential growth of 4-5% lost versus the prior plan.
India revenue (about 4% of total) expected to roughly double in FY27; medium-term target of double-digit annualised growth.
Truck and off-highway spend expected to pick up in H2 CY2026 with pre-buying; management expects the T40 account base to become more balanced across segments.
capex_capacity: R&D investment held at above 5% of revenue, with partner and acquisition investments (about $400 million cited) on top of that.
Ecosystem partnerships with Qualcomm, Microsoft, Qorix (middleware), Helm.ai (autonomy), Pathpartner, Technica, Cymotive and Caresoft.
Beacon AI platform used internally across about 13,000 staff and licensable as a product.
Two new Chinese OEM engagements won; China presence refreshed, with revenue still small.
New partnership with Hero Motors for micromobility, launched from India.
demand_pricing: Management said it had about 10-11% market share and that wallet share among the top 25 clients (T25) was about 10% last year, targeted to rise to 15-20%.
More than 80% of new contracts are fixed-price; four of the largest clients to convert to outcome-based models in Q4 and the next four in Q1 FY27, taking that share above 75%.
Added 13 new clients in FY26 (4 truck, 6 off-highway, 3 passenger car OEMs), with a large North American off-highway OEM awarding a SDV program.
OEM spend outlook: McKinsey data (Jan 2026) shows automotive R&D spend growing about 2x by 2030, led by AD/ADAS (about 3x); management said its addressable share is smaller.
Management said no OEM has yet cut spending due to the Middle East conflict and oil prices, though a conflict beyond 3-6 months could hit trucks first.

qa_highlights.question: How will AD/ADAS progress for a legacy supplier when much of the new spend goes to new-age OEMs?
qa_highlights.answer: Kishor said legacy OEMs are sourcing autonomy from new partners (e.g. Momenta, Helm), and KPIT's opportunity is validation and simulation, plus off-highway autonomy.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue gap to cover in FY27 from the 4-5% sequential growth lost to program ramp-down?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the impact is 3-4% of quarterly revenue, starting Q1 FY27, and it expects to cover it with pipeline in existing clients and new accounts.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the move to a 22-24% EBITDA margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Products and solutions carry higher gross margins, reusable assets and AI-infused work improve margins, fixed-price conversion helps, and AI lowers SG&A.

qa_highlights.question: How does KPIT compete with Chinese automotive engineering firms that run lower margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Kishor said KPIT competes favourably outside China and already sells products to top China OEMs; Sachin said China's advantage is EV platforms and batteries, which are complementary.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 TCV jump, and is that repeatable?
qa_highlights.answer: Kishor said the jump came from off-highway commercial wins and traditional clients; Sachin said quarterly variability is normal but half-yearly and yearly TCV is growing.

qa_highlights.question: Do European and North American OEMs plan to increase SDV spend?
qa_highlights.answer: Sachin said European OEMs are focused on cutting cost and reconsidering partners, creating opportunities, while US OEMs are investing in next-generation SDVs.

risks_watch: Revenue loss from the two SDV program ramp-downs (one a planned European OEM program, one a Japanese OEM program stopped near production) hits Q1 FY27, with 3-4% quarterly impact.
Delivery of FY27 EBITDA guidance of 20.5-21.2% while investing in AI and new markets, with currency swings a stated risk.
Pace of solutions and products growth (30% target) and conversion of the four largest clients to outcome-based contracts in Q4 and Q1.
Middleware (Qorix) and autonomous driving revenue delayed by architecture program slippage, with a 1-2 year lag.
Macro risk: Middle East conflict and oil prices could affect truck and off-highway spend if they persist beyond 3-6 months.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the medium-term story and pipeline, but cautious on near-term revenue after the program ramp-downs. Management was more open than usual about the surprise OEM program stop and was reticent on the names and size of specific accounts.
key_quotes: So, it challenged near-term growth, but expanded foundation for substantial future expansion.
We expect 30% year-on-year revenue growth in solution and products, and we hope it will increase over the period.
More than 80% of our new contracts are fixed price in nature.

growth.why: Management guides solutions and products revenue up about 30% YoY in FY27 and FY27 EBITDA margin of 20.5-21.2%, backed by $349M Q4 TCV, 13 new clients and 80%+ fixed-price contracts, but no specific capacity is cited and the two large SDV ramp-downs weigh on Q1 FY27 by an estimated 3-4% QoQ.
